arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Frederick argued that Congress enacted ERISA to impose the highest known fiduciary duty.
Mr. Garre argued that this case is part of a wave of lawsuits aimed at changing fiduciary practices through damages.
Mr. Huston argued that ERISA text requires administrators to act with care, skill, prudence, and diligence.
Mr. Frederick urged the Court to remand the case because the lower court treated it as a motion to dismiss.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of fiduciary duties under ERISA. the sides that brought the case argue that selecting expensive funds violates the duty of prudence. The university contends that courts should not second-guess investment choices through retroactive damages claims.

paragraphs: The outcome defines the standard for selecting retirement plan investments. It determines whether plan administrators face personal liability for choosing higher-cost funds. This affects the financial security of millions of workers and the structure of university retirement plans.
